title: api: standardize rate-limit semantics, idempotency, retry-after for streaming, tool-calls, and OpenAI-compat
author: Maya Lin
description: Motivation: customer-facing instability around streaming responses and tool/function-calling surface exposed different rate-limit and retry semantics than our OpenAI-compat layer. This caused confusing 429 vs 503 behaviors, duplicated tool invocations on retries, and inconsistent Retry-After headers between streaming and non-streaming endpoints. This PR unifies rate-limit headers and retry behavior across the text/chat/streaming endpoints, hardens idempotency handling for streaming+tool calls, and updates the OpenAI-compat layer so third-party SDKs see consistent error codes and Retry-After semantics. Summary of changes: 1) Standardize rate-limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset and compat variants) and ensure they are sent for streaming responses (both initial response and in final event). 2) Enforce Retry-After semantics for 429/503 responses from routing layer and surface Retry-After in OpenAI-compat responses. 3) Implement streaming-aware idempotency: server persists idempotency-key for in-flight streaming requests, and retries with the same key will be rejected with a consistent 409 conflict or 202 in-progress response instead of re-executing tool calls. 4) Protect function/tool calling: tool invocations are keyed by request-id+function-signature to deduplicate side-effectful calls on retry paths. 5) Update error response shape to include standardized error.code, error.type, and error.param where applicable to match OpenAI semantics. 6) Add comprehensive unit/integration tests and a migration note in docs. Backwards compatibility: all OpenAI-compat clients will get more consistent error codes and Retry-After headers; no breaking API changes expected but behavior around duplicate side-effects is tightened (idempotent by default when idempotency-key provided). See release notes for guidance.

release_notes:
- Standardized rate-limit headers and Retry-After semantics across text, chat, and streaming endpoints.
- Streaming responses now include rate-limit headers and a final Retry-After when applicable.
- Server-side streaming idempotency: providing an idempotency-key prevents duplicate tool/function calls on retries.
- OpenAI-compat layer now exposes consistent error.code and error.type fields and includes retry_after in response bodies for 429/503.
- Added integration tests and docs for rate-limits and idempotency. Refer to docs/api/rate_limits.md and docs/api/idempotency.md for migration guidance.
notes_for_support: Support teams: If customers report duplicate tool side-effects for streaming requests, ask for the idempotency-key and request-id; with the new behavior, we will dedupe when idempotency-key is present. For older clients without keys, document best-effort dedupe and recommend client-side idempotency keys. If customers see Retry-After inconsistencies, confirm that they are hitting the updated routing layer; ask for request timestamps and headers. Linked ticket SUP-887 contains a repro harness.
